paper.title: SERF: Spatiotemporal Environment and Robot Feature Map for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Long-horizon mobile-manipulation VLA study using an explicit spatiotemporal scene-and-robot memory.

sections_read.purpose: Identify partial observability and memory limits in long-horizon mobile manipulation.
Inspect the neural point-map representation and updates.
Record privileged mapping and simulation boundaries.

research_question: Can an explicit spatiotemporal map improve VLA policies on long-horizon mobile manipulation under partial observability?
contributions: A map-conditioned VLA using a joint spatiotemporal neural point representation of scene and robot state.

method.summary: SERF builds and updates a neural point map of objects, environment and robot, then conditions a fine-tuned VLA on retrieved map tokens.
assumptions: Instance-aware mappings and stable rigid-object tracking are available.
A prior scene map can be constructed or maintained.

study_context.sample_or_scale: Three BEHAVIOR-1K tasks with repeated simulation evaluations.

evaluation.design: SERF is compared with pretrained and fine-tuned image-only VLA baselines; map-token and configuration ablations are reported.

findings.finding: Explicit scene-and-robot memory improved task progress on all three evaluated long-horizon tasks over the fine-tuned image-only VLA.

author_stated.limitation: The experiments are simulated and rely on privileged instance labels, prior maps and rigid-motion assumptions.

reader_inferred.boundary: The result demonstrates value of structured memory, not readiness for online real-world mapping.
reader_inferred.basis: Mapping inputs and labels are privileged and no hardware experiments are reported.

transfer_boundary: Supports explicit memory for simulated long-horizon tasks; real perception and map maintenance remain unvalidated.

design_strengths: Direct comparison against the same VLA with and without map conditioning.
Evaluates multiple long-horizon tasks and map ablations.
design_risks: Privileged maps and labels simplify the hardest perception problem.
Only three tasks and no hardware.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: The fine-tuned image-only baseline shares the VLA backbone and task data.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Task progress captures partial completion, though it can reward incomplete plans.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Map and policy details are documented in appendices.

evidence_cards.claim: Across three simulated BEHAVIOR-1K tasks, SERF achieved mean task progress of 63.5, 60.1 and 52.5, versus 40.7, 43.0 and 48.4 for the fine-tuned image-only PI0.5 baseline.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports explicit spatiotemporal memory for long-horizon mobile manipulation, subject to real-world mapping validation.
evidence_cards.summary: The main table reports mean task progress for the full system and image-only baseline across three tasks.
evidence_cards.source_context: The full SERF policy achieves the highest task progress on all three evaluated tasks.

verification.rationale: The table row contains the three means and standard deviations for both methods.
